title: NSS servers: the VM record, its certificate, platforms and Nanolog capacity

prose.label: Managing it.
prose.text: {{servers-page}} The feeds a server carries are in [[shared.nss.feeds]].
Cloud & Branch Connector NSS deployments have their own server and feed limits: [[cloud-connector.nss-va]].

checks.do: Whether the NSS VM holds the client certificate issued for its server record.
For a high-volume tenant, how many Nanolog clusters it has, since each needs its own NSS VM server.

server-record.statement: An NSS server is the representation of the NSS VM in the Admin Console; after a server is created, Zscaler issues a client certificate and private key to install on the NSS VM so that it can authenticate to the Zscaler service.

quotes: An NSS server is the representation of the NSS virtual machine (VM) in the Zscaler Admin Console. After you create a server, Zscaler issues a client certificate and private key that you can install on the NSS VM so that it can authenticate to the Zscaler service.

appliance-platforms.statement: VM-based NSS requires a virtual appliance; deployment guides cover Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, Hyper-V, Microsoft Azure, Nutanix and VMware vSphere, and the architecture is the same whichever is used.

quotes: Requires a virtual appliance for deployment.

NSS Deployment Guide for Amazon Web Services - NSS Deployment Guide for Google Cloud Platform - NSS Deployment Guide for Hyper-V - NSS Deployment Guide for Microsoft Azure - NSS Deployment Guide for Nutanix - NSS Deployment Guide for VMware vSphere
The architecture remains the same regardless of the deployment method selected.

auto-update.statement: After deployment the NSS requires minimal administration and automatically polls the Zscaler service for updates and installs them.

quotes: After deployment, the NSS requires minimal administration and automatically polls the Zscaler service for updates and installs them.

servers-page.statement: The NSS Servers page lets an administrator add a server, deploy an NSS virtual appliance, download MIB files, and download or add an SSL certificate for a server; it lists each server's name, type, status and health state.

quotes: Download the SSL Certificate for an NSS server.
Add a new SSL Certificate for an NSS Server.
Server Name: The name of the server.
State: The health state of the server.

nanolog-capacity.statement: A Nanolog cluster is listed at 1 billion web transactions, beyond which additional Nanolog clusters are required; an NSS VM server takes 1 Nanolog cluster, so additional clusters require an adequate number of NSS VM servers.

quotes: | Number of Web Transactions per Nanolog Cluster | 1 billion web transactions | If your organization surpasses more than 1 billion web transactions, additional Nanolog clusters are required. |

| Number of Nanolog Clusters per NSS Virtual Machine (VM) Server | 1 Nanolog cluster | If additional Nanolog clusters are required, your organization must support an adequate number of NSS VM servers. |

scale-out.statement: A tenant whose web traffic needs more than one Nanolog cluster also needs at least one NSS VM server per cluster for a VM-based NSS export to cover all of it.
scale-out.conditions: Follows from one cluster per NSS VM server; the help does not say how a tenant's logs are divided between clusters or over what period the transaction count is measured.
